annotations.annotation_text: The nocturnal oneiric dimension (night): Joyce's exploration of the sleeping body, sensory deprivation, auditory distortions, and the somatic language of the collective unconscious.
sources: Bishop, John. Joyce's Book of the Dark. https://archive.org/details/joycesbookofdark0000bish
Freud, Sigmund. The Interpretation of Dreams. https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/4349

annotations.annotation_text: Mythological and folkloric archetype (Patrick): invoking the ancient Fianna cycle, heroic legends of Ireland, and the patron saints of early Celtic Christianity.
sources: MacKillop, James. Dictionary of Celtic Mythology. https://www.oxfordreference.com
Lady Gregory. Gods and Fighting Men. https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/14465

annotations.annotation_text: Universal archetype of the father and everyman protagonist Humphrey Chimpden Earwicker (HCE), manifested here as "porter". Represents the recumbent Dublin landscape with head at Howth and body stretching west to Phoenix Park.
sources: Glasheen, Adaline. Third Census of Finnegans Wake. https://archive.org/details/thirdcensusoffin0000glas
McHugh, Roland. The Sigla of Finnegans Wake. https://archive.org/details/siglaoffinnegans0000mchu
James Joyce Digital Archive: Finnegans Wake Notons. https://jjda.ie

annotations.annotation_text: Joyce's recurring mystical or structural number (four): encoding cabalistic intervals, Viconian divisions, and historical Dublin dates.
sources: Hart, Clive. Structure and Motif in Finnegans Wake. https://archive.org/details/structuremotifin0000hart
McHugh, Roland. Annotations to Finnegans Wake. https://archive.org/details/annotationstofin0000mchu_h5g8
